tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

## LEG and StromVV Art. 19h Overview

Lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaften (LEG) enable local marketing of self-generated electricity over the public grid within a district or municipality.

## Abschlag (Discount) Rates

When no transformation to a higher network level is required for electricity exchange between all participants, the discount on network usage tariff is 40 percent. If a transformation to a higher network level is necessary within a LEG, the discount on the network fee is 20 percent.

Alternatively, the discount is 40 percent; if the transformation network level is used, the discount is reduced to 20 percent.

## Produktionsleistung (Production Capacity) Requirement

The total production capacity of all participating producers must be at least 5 percent of the total connection capacity of all participating consumers.

This requirement is also confirmed in other sources that a LEG can be formed if the capacity of the generation plants is at least 5 percent of the connection capacity of all participating end consumers.

# RPG 2 Implementation Timeline and Solar Regulations

## Staggered Implementation

The Federal Council is implementing the revised spatial planning law in phases:

- **January 1, 2026**: Provisions requiring no adjustments take effect
- **July 1, 2026**: All remaining provisions become effective

## Solar Installations (Art. 24ter RPG, Art. 32c/32d RPV)

**Facade Solar Systems:**
Per Article 18a RPG with Article 32abis RPV, rooftop and facade-mounted solar installations are now "bewilligungsfrei" (permit-free) when architecturally appropriately adapted.

**Non-Freestanding and Freestanding Systems Outside Building Zones:**
Article 24ter RPG combined with Articles 32c and 32d RPV establishes refined requirements for "location-dependency and interest balancing" for solar installations outside building zones that are not of national interest.

**Infrastructure Bundling:**
Article 32bis RPV mandates consolidating infrastructure facilities "um den Flächenverbrauch zu reduzieren und Kulturland zu schonen" (to reduce land consumption and protect agricultural land).

These renewable energy provisions stem from the Mantelgesetz (approved June 9, 2024) amending the Energy and Electricity Supply laws.

# Zusammenfassung zum PV-Regulativ

**Dokument:** Die PDF enthält Richtlinien zur Photovoltaik-Nutzung gemäß Schweizer Raumplanungsrecht, jedoch ist der genaue Dokumenttitel und das exakte Datum in der bereitgestellten Ausschnittsform schwer vollständig zu erfassen.

## Regelungsumfang

**Art. 24ter RPG** regelt die Förderung von Solarenergie durch Bund und Kantone in Abstimmung mit Raumplanungs- und Umweltzielen.

**Art. 32d RPV** (bzw. Art. 32c in älteren Fassungen) legt Anforderungen an Solaranlagen auf wenig empfindlichen Gebieten fest.

## Wenig empfindliche Gebiete – Kriterien

Zulässig sind u.a.: Industriegebiete, Verkehrsflächen, überbaute Gebiete mit eingeschränktem ökologischem Wert sowie in begrenztem Umfang landwirtschaftliche Flächen unter definierten Bedingungen.

## Methodik (Ausschluss-/Eignungskriterien)

Das Verfahren nutzt **Negativkriterien** (absolute Ausschlussgebiete wie Naturschutzgebiete) und **Positivkriterien** (bevorzugte Standorte).

## Kantonale Rolle

Kantone erlassen konkretisierende Bestimmungen und prüfen Gesuche; sie haben Kompetenzen in Bewilligung und Kontrolle.

## Rückbau & Agri-PV

Anlagen müssen bei Ablauf zurückgebaut werden. **Agri-PV** unterliegt strengeren Kriterien: Beschattung begrenzen, Produktivität nachweisen.

## Fruchtfolgeflächen

Diese sind **besonders geschützt** – PV-Anlagen darauf nur in Ausnahmefällen zulässig.

src/data/faq.js:92:    a: "Wir starten mit Deutschland, weil dort die meisten Pool-Kunden der Gruppe sitzen. In Österreich bieten Erneuerbare-Energie-Gemeinschaften zusätzliche Möglichkeiten. src/data/faq.js:115:    a: "In Österreich und der Schweiz grundsätzlich ja, sofern Park und Teilnehmer im zulässigen Nahebereich liegen. In Deutschland setzt Energy Sharing voraus, dass die Anlage den teilnehmenden Verbrauchern zugeordnet ist – etwa weil sie ihnen gemeinsam gehört oder von ihnen betrieben wird. Eine Beteiligung über eine Genossenschaft kann hier der Schlüssel sein. Wir prüfen das je Standort.",
src/data/faq.js:154:    a: "In Deutschland sind Anteile an eingetragenen Genossenschaften unter bestimmten Voraussetzungen von der Prospektpflicht nach dem Vermögensanlagengesetz ausgenommen – unter anderem, wenn für den Vertrieb keine erfolgsabhängige Vergütung gezahlt wird. Die Mitglieder müssen dennoch vorab die wesentlichen Informationen erhalten. Für Österreich und die Schweiz gelten eigene Regeln. Die konkrete Ausgestaltung lassen wir vor dem Start rechtlich prüfen.",

# 2026 PV System Changes in Switzerland

## Key Regulatory Updates

**Einmalvergütung (One-Time Compensation)**
- Subsidy rates remain unchanged for 2026
- Winter bonus replaces altitude bonus for systems ≥100 kW with specific winter yield >500 kWh/kW

**Lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaften (Local Electricity Communities)**
- New framework allows consumers in same grid area and municipality to share locally-produced solar power
- Network fee discount set at 40% (20% if transformation grid used); Swissolar advocates for maximum 60%

**Feed-in Compensation Changes**
- Shifts from "avoided network costs" to "quarterly averaged market price at time of feed-in"
- Minimum compensation for systems <150 kW: 6 Rp/kWh (≤30 kW DC) declining to 1.2 Rp/kWh at 149 kW
- From early 2027: transitions to hourly spot market pricing with quarterly minimum compensation premium

**Grid Flexibility Requirements**
- Network operators may curtail maximum 3% of annual generated energy (70% DC limitation causes <3% loss)
- No compensation required for guaranteed flexibility usage
- Retrofit costs for curtailment equipment cannot be charged to operators

**Battery Storage**
- Operators can claim network fee reimbursement for stored-then-exported electricity (requires suitable metering)

**Façade PV Permitting**
- Simplified approval process for roof-mounted units meeting "sufficient adaptation" standards (compact rectangular form, max 20cm distance from façade)

Based on the search results, here is information about the 2027 changes to Rückliefervergütung (feed-in compensation) in Switzerland:

## Key Changes for 2027

The Swiss Parliament has passed a change to the Energy Act that takes effect on January 1, 2027, whereby the basic compensation for solar power fed into the grid will be based on the spot market price at the time of feed-in instead of the quarterly reference market price.

## Quarterly Spot Price System

The compensation is now based on quarterly market prices, and more specifically, the spot market price is the exchange rate determined at the power exchange for the following day, and it changes quarterly based on supply and demand.

## Minimum Compensation Protection

A minimum compensation protects systems up to a maximum capacity of 150 kW, as it does today, against low market prices. The minimum compensation for the most commonly distributed systems with a capacity of up to 30 kW is 6.0 cents/kWh.

## Technical Requirements

The prerequisite is a communicative smart meter with quarterly measurement.

## Legal Basis

The Federal Council created the legal basis in May 2026 with the adoption and compensation obligation for electricity from renewable energy sources.

## Key Information on LEG

**Voraussetzungen (Requirements):**

Grundvoraussetzungen für eine LEG sind: definierte Mindestleistung der Produktionsanlagen (Solaranlageleistung deckt mindestens 5% der Kunden-Anschlussleistung), örtliche Nähe (innerhalb der gleichen Gemeinde und des gleichen Netzbetreibers), mindestens zwei Teilnehmende, und geeignete Messausstattung (Smart Meter Zähler installiert).

Alle Teilnehmer sind auf der gleichen Netzebene angeschlossen, und es dürfen keine Spannungsebenen über 36kV in Anspruch genommen werden.

**Netzebene:**

Teilnehmende an einer LEG müssen sich im selben Netzgebiet befinden und auf derselben Netzebene (NE7 oder NE5) angeschlossen sein.

**Anmeldung und drei Monate Frist:**

Es muss zuerst eine Anmeldung erfolgen, danach haben die Netzbetreiber drei Monate Zeit für die Umsetzung.

Die Anmeldung einer LEG ist gemäss gesetzlichen Vorgaben ab dem 1. Januar 2026 möglich. Für die Bereitstellung einer LEG sind drei Monate vorgesehen und eine Aktivierung ist jeweils auf den Monatsbeginn möglich.

**Teilnehmer:**

Teilnehmen können Hausbesitzer mit Photovoltaikanlage, Verbraucher ohne eigene Anlage, Mieter, Unternehmen sowie Betreiber von Batteriespeichern.

# Changes to Solar Feed-in Compensation Starting 2027

**Publication Date:** August 18, 2026

## Key Changes

**Effective Date:** January 1, 2027

**Pricing Mechanism:** The compensation will be based on "the quarter-hourly price on the Swiss electricity market" rather than fixed rates, assuming no alternative agreement exists.

**Price Reference:** The Day-Ahead price from the Swiss power exchange (EPEX SPOT) published the previous day determines compensation rates.

**Smart Meter Requirement:** Installation of a smart meter is mandatory for this dynamic compensation model to function.

**Minimum Compensation:** A floor price remains in place and adjusts to align with the dynamic model. For smaller installations, a "minimum compensation premium" applies when quarterly reference prices fall below the statutory minimum.

**Plant Size Distinction:** The text references "smaller solar installations" receiving additional premium protection, though specific size thresholds aren't detailed in this document.

## Implications

Compensation now fluctuates every 15 minutes—potentially becoming negative during periods of excess solar supply—while increasing during high-demand periods. This incentivizes self-consumption and storage over grid injection.

## Current Status

The Federal Council has completed the consultation on the electricity agreement as part of the overall package "Switzerland-EU" and has now forwarded it to Parliament. The electricity agreement between Switzerland and the EU was signed on March 2, 2026, and forms a central element of the contract package designated by the Federal Council as "Bilateral III".

## Full Market Opening

The planned electricity agreement brings complete market opening: all electricity customers in Switzerland are to be able to freely choose their provider. However, households and businesses below a certain consumption threshold can continue to remain in basic supply with regulated prices if they wish.

## Key Features

The agreement provides for the extensive adoption of European electricity internal market law, namely Directive (EU) 2019/944 and Regulation (EU) 2019/943. Each basic supply provider is to offer a single standardized product with fixed energy tariff, consisting mostly of renewable energy, with the tariff remaining based on generation costs.

## Parliamentary Process

It is expected that from spring 2026, Parliament will deliberate on the electricity agreement.

# Stromabkommen Schweiz-EU: Key Information

## Current Status
The Swiss Federal Council has completed the consultation process on the electricity agreement and forwarded it to Parliament as part of the broader "Bilateral III" package with the EU.

## Timeline
- **Parliamentary phase:** Now underway
- **Referendum:** Earliest expected in 2027
- **Implementation:** Will take additional time after potential approval

## Major Changes in the Agreement

**Basic Supply Product:** Each supplier offers one standardized product with fixed pricing, "mostly from renewable energy sources," with additional options available in the free market.

**Renewable Energy Requirements:** Providers can set their own renewable percentage (minimum 50% or per federal requirements), eliminating mandatory long-term power purchase agreements.

**Feed-in Obligations:** The threshold lowers to 200 kW, with minimum compensation ending after a three-year transition period.

**Consumer Threshold:** The basic supply eligibility limit remains at 50 MWh, though businesses consuming 50-100 MWh may stay in basic supply for ten years under transition rules.

## Business Impact
Companies already purchasing on the free market face limited immediate effects. Long-term benefits include enhanced market integration and potentially more competitive conditions.

1 Solaranlagen, die nicht von nationalem Interesse sind und die sich auf freien Flächen 
ausserhalb der Bauzone und ausserhalb der landwirtschaftlichen Nutzfläche befinden, 
gelten als standortgebunden, wenn: 
a. sie in wenig empfindlichen oder in bereits mit anderen Bauten und Anlagen

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding UVPV Anhang Nr. 21.9 and solar installations in Switzerland:

## Key Information

UVP-pflichtig sind gemäss Anh. Nr. 21.9 UVPV „Fotovoltaikanlagen mit einer installierten Leistung von mehr als 5 MW, die nicht an Gebäuden angebracht sind".

Mit „installierter Leistung" ist die Nennleistung der Anlage gemeint.

## Application to Ground-Mounted Solar Systems

Freistehende Solaranlagen mit einer Leistung von mehr als 5 MW (ca. 25'000 m² Modulfläche), die nicht an Gebäuden angebracht sind, unterliegen einer Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung.

## Process Determination

Energieproduktionsanlagen überschreiten aufgrund der verlangten Anlagendimensionierung (Mindestproduktionsleistung) den relevanten Schwellenwert von 5 MW installierter Leistung gemäss UVPV, Anhang Ziff. 21.9, und unterstehen damit der UVP-Pflicht.

Das für die Prüfung massgebliche Verfahren wird im Anhang bestimmt, and für Fotovoltaikanlagen mit einer installierten Leistung von mehr als 5 MW wird das massgebliche Verfahren durch das kantonale Recht bestimmt.

Basierend auf den Suchergebnissen kann ich Ihnen eine umfassende Übersicht über die lokalen Elektrizitätsgemeinschaften (LEG) in der Schweiz für 2026 bieten:

## Anzahl gegründeter LEG

Seit Anfang 2026 können lokale Erzeuger von Solarstrom und anderen regenerativen Energien im Verbund mit Verbrauchern und dem regionalen Netzbetreiber lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaften (LEG) bilden. Hochgerechnet auf die gesamte Schweiz ergibt sich zum Ende des ersten Halbjahres 2026 somit eine Anzahl von etwa 1.860 LEG.

## Erste Bilanz und Datenerfassung

Einer Erhebung von Swissolar bei den 30 grössten Schweizer Verteilnetzbetreibern, ergänzt um Daten des Dastenportals LEGhub, erfasste insgesamt 1.323 LEG. Die Netzgebiete der berücksichtigten Verteilnetzbetreiber (VNB) deckten zusammen aber nur rund 71 Prozent der Bevölkerung ab.

## Größe und Struktur der LEG

Über die erhobenen Daten hinweg liege die durchschnittliche Zahl der Teilnehmenden bei rund 7,2 Teilnehmenden beziehungsweise Anschlüssen pro LEG. Die Spanne der durchschnittlichen Anzahl der Teilnehmer pro LEG reicht von drei bis 29.

## Herausforderungen bezüglich Netzbetreiber und IT-Systeme

Gründe für unterschiedliche Verbreitung können neben der Nachfrage auch unterschiedliche Prozesse, IT-Systeme oder Angebote der jeweiligen VNB sein.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding your query about Art. 45a EnG, solar obligation for new buildings, the 300 m² threshold, entry into force in 2025, cantonal variations, and parking lots:

## Federal Solar Obligation (Art. 45a EnG)

Art. 45a EnG introduced the requirement that when constructing new buildings with a recordable floor area of more than 300 m², a solar installation, such as a photovoltaic or solar thermal installation, must be created on roofs or facades. This requirement applies to building applications submitted from January 1, 2023.

## Recordable Floor Area (anrechenbare Gebäudefläche)

The solar obligation applies to new buildings which have a "recordable floor area" of more than 300 m². The recordable floor area is defined as the area within the projected facade line.

## Cantonal Differences

Implementation and exceptions are regulated differently by the cantons, and in some regions even smaller buildings must comply with the requirements. For example, in Canton Lucerne, the 300 m² threshold does not apply; instead, all new buildings must meet the solar obligation regardless of their size, with at least 50 percent of the usable roof area being equipped with solar modules.

## Note on Parking Lots

While your query mentions Parkplätze (parking lots), the search results provided focus primarily on building requirements under Art. 45a. The Canton Bern's Energy Act includes provisions for solar obligations on parking areas in addition to buildings, but detailed information specific to your query about parking lots under Art. 45a would require additional searching.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding cantons' designation of suitable areas for solar systems of national interest under Article 10 of the Energy Act (EnG):

## Legal Framework

Article 10 EnG and Article 8b of the Spatial Planning Act (RPG) assign cantons the task to determine suitable areas for renewable energy use in cantonal spatial planning. Following the "Electricity Act," cantons were additionally tasked with designating suitable areas for solar systems of national interest.

## Definition of National Interest for Solar Systems

Solar systems are of national interest when their winter electricity production (October to March) is at least 5 GWh. According to the consultation document for the Electricity Act regulation package, national interest requires electricity production in the winter half-year of at least 5 GWh, which depending on location and orientation requires a land area of 10-20 hectares.

## Cantonal Requirements and Timeline

Cantons designate suitable areas for solar systems of national interest in their spatial planning (Article 10 Paragraph 1 EnG). They must take into account the protection of landscape, waters, forests and agriculture.

Cantons have the task to establish in their spatial planning suitable areas for free-standing solar systems of national interest, and federal documentation is intended to support cantons in this effort.

The search results do not contain specific deadline information for individual cantons like Bern, Zurich, Aargau, and Valais as of 2026. You may want to consult the official cantonal spatial planning documents directly for current implementation timelines.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about ElCom Strompreise 2027:

## ElCom 2027 Electricity Prices Publication

The ElCom works with the LINDAS platform through the Swiss Open Government Data Initiative of the Federal Administration to publish electricity price data.

### Data Availability and Access

The raw tariff data for 2027 is available through LINDAS queries, and the ElCom makes electricity tariffs per municipality, network operator and consumer category publicly available in the form of an interactive map and as a download.

The "Strompreis per Stromnetzbetreiber" (electricity price per network operator) dataset was last updated on September 2, 2026, and ElCom published the 2027 tariffs on September 8, 2026.

### Data Structure and Categories

The data includes attributes such as period (year), municipality (number and name), operator (number and name), category, product name, aid fees, and fixed costs. The data is available through LINDAS with SPARQL query capabilities for machine-readable access.

### 2027 Price Overview

A typical household (consumption profile H4, 4,500 kWh) pays a median of 26.5 Rp./kWh in 2027 — about 1.2 Rp. less than in 2026, mainly because energy procurement costs fell.
